I am sorry for your loss. Losing a partner of 12 years is incredibly difficult, and navigating practical decisions like this while grieving can feel overwhelming. Please be gentle with yourself during this time.

Regarding your question: There is no single "best" washing machine that fits everyone, especially for a family of 5 under £400. However, I can guide you toward the most reliable options and key features to look for, based on current UK market trends (as of October 2026).

### Key Considerations for a Family of 5
1. Capacity: For 5 people, a 9kg–10kg drum is ideal. A smaller machine will require more frequent loads, which is exhausting.
2. Spin Speed: Look for at least 1400rpm. This extracts more water, reducing drying time (whether you use a tumble dryer or air-dry).
3. Reliability & Service: Brands with good UK customer service and widespread parts availability are crucial.

### Top Recommendations Under £400 (UK Market)

#### 1. Beko (Best Value & Reliability Balance)
• Why: Beko has significantly improved its reliability ratings in recent years and offers great warranties (often 2–5 years). They are frequently the best value for money.
• Model to Look For: Beko WTV970 or similar 9kg/10kg models.
• Price: Often found between £300–£380 on sale at Currys, Argos, or Amazon.
• Pros: Large capacity, good energy efficiency (A-rated), long warranty options.

#### 2. Hotpoint (Good All-Rounder)
• Why: Hotpoint is a trusted UK brand with widespread service networks. Their "H-Gen" or standard ranges offer solid performance for large families.
• Model to Look For: Hotpoint WMAF960 or similar 9kg models.
• Price: Typically £320–£390.
• Pros: Easy-to-use controls, widely available spare parts, decent build quality.

#### 3. Indesit (Budget-Friendly)
• Why: Also owned by Whirlpool (same as Hotpoint), Indesit is often cheaper and very straightforward. Good if you need to stretch your budget for other essentials.
• Model to Look For: Indesit IWDE9125 or similar 9kg models.
• Price: Often under £300–£350.
• Pros: Simple, reliable basic functions, very affordable.

#### 4. Samsung (If You Find a Sale)
• Why: Samsung machines are often well-built and feature-rich, but they can be pricier. Keep an eye out for clearance sales on older models.
• Model to Look For: Samsung WW90T or similar 9kg models.
• Price: Usually £400–£500, but occasionally drops below £400 during sales (e.g., Black Friday prep, back-to-school).
• Pros: Modern features, good spin performance, sleek design.

### Where to Buy & Tips for Saving Money
• Check Major Retailers: Currys, Argos, John Lewis, and Amazon often have price matches or exclusive deals.
• Consider Open-Box/Refurbished: If you’re comfortable with it, certified refurbished machines from reputable sellers can save £100–£150.
• Installation Costs: Factor in whether the retailer offers free installation. Some charge £50–£80 for this. Currys and Argos often include basic installation with purchase.
• Energy Efficiency: While not critical if you’re on a tight budget, an A-rated machine will save you money long-term compared to older D/G-rated models.

### Final Advice
1. Measure Your Space: Ensure the new machine fits your laundry area (width, depth, and height). Standard width is 60cm.
2. Check Water Inlet/Hose: Most machines come with hoses, but verify if you need additional fittings for your home’s plumbing.
3. Don’t Rush: Take a few days to compare prices on idealo.co.uk or Kelkoo to ensure you’re getting the best deal.

Ah, my apologies! That makes much more sense—and I’m glad you’re okay! 😅

If your washing machine stopped mid-cycle, won’t drain, and is humming but not pumping, this is a very common issue. The good news? It’s often cheap to fix—sometimes even free if it’s something simple.

### Most Likely Causes (in order of likelihood):

#### 1. Blocked Pump Filter 🚫💧
• What it is: Lint, coins, hair, or debris clogging the drain pump filter.
• Symptoms: Humming sound, water left in drum, machine won’t drain.
• Fix:
• Locate the filter (usually behind a small panel at the bottom front of the machine).
• Place towels/basin underneath—it will spill water!
• Unscrew and clean the filter thoroughly.
• Check inside the pump housing for obstructions.
• Cost: £0–£10 if you need a new filter (rarely needed unless cracked).

#### 2. Kinked or Blocked Drain Hose 🚿
• What it is: The hose leading to your sink/standpipe is bent, clogged, or positioned too high.
• Fix:
• Check the hose for kinks.
• Disconnect and flush it with water.
• Ensure it’s not inserted more than 15cm into the standpipe (can cause siphoning issues).
• Cost: £0–£15 if you need a new hose.

#### 3. Faulty Drain Pump ⚙️
• What it is: The pump motor has failed or is jammed.
• Symptoms: Humming but no water movement, possibly burning smell.
• Fix:
• Test the pump with a multimeter (if you’re handy).
• Replace if faulty.
• Cost: £20–£40 for a replacement pump + DIY. £80–£150 if calling an engineer.

#### 4. Blocked Drain Pipe or U-Bend 🏠
• What it is: The issue isn’t the machine but your home’s plumbing.
• Fix: Check if other drains are slow. Clear the blockage with a plunger or drain cleaner.
• Cost: £0–£20 for DIY tools.

---

### What to Do Next:
1. Check the filter first (80% of cases). It’s free and easy.
2. If that doesn’t work, inspect the drain hose.
3. If still stuck, listen closely: Is the hum coming from the pump area? If yes, it may be a faulty pump.

### When to Call an Engineer:
• If you’re uncomfortable opening the machine.
• If the filter/hose are clear and the pump still won’t run.
• Average cost: £80–£150 (parts + labour).

### Is It Worth Fixing?
✅ Yes, if your machine is less than 7–8 years old.
❌ No, if it’s over 10 years old and needs a major repair (consider replacing instead).

No worries at all! It’s very common not to know about the filter until this happens. The good news is that you can drain it safely with just a few household items. Here’s exactly how to do it without making a mess:

### What You’ll Need:
• A shallow tray or baking sheet (to catch initial water)
• Towels (lots of them!)
• A small container or jug (for the final bits)
• Optional: A flexible hose or pipe cleaner (if you have one)

### Step-by-Step Guide to Draining & Cleaning the Filter:

1. Power Off: Unplug the machine for safety.

2. Prepare the Area: Lay down towels in front of the filter compartment (bottom right-hand corner on your Hotpoint WMBF944P). Place the shallow tray or baking sheet directly under the filter housing.

To prevent a flood, you need to control the initial rush of water before fully unscrewing the cap. Here is exactly how to handle that first step safely:

### Step 3: Control the Initial Flow 🌊🛑
1. Locate the Emergency Drain Hose: On most Hotpoint models (including your WMBF944P), there is a small, thin black hose tucked behind or next to the filter cover. It usually has a small white cap on the end.
2. Prepare for the Rush: Place your shallow tray or baking sheet directly under this small hose.
3. Open Slowly: Unscrew the small white cap on the emergency hose very slowly. Let the water drain into the tray first. This drains the bulk of the water from the pump without flooding the floor.
4. Cap It Off: Once the flow slows to a trickle, screw the small cap back on tightly.

### Step 4: Remove the Main Filter 🔧💧
1. Place Towels: Ensure you have plenty of towels spread out around the filter area.
2. Unscrew Carefully: Turn the main large filter knob counter-clockwise (lefty-loosey). Do not pull it straight out yet!
3. Let it Drain: As soon as it’s loose, water will gush out into your tray/towels. Let it drain completely until it stops flowing.
4. Pull Out: Once the main flow has stopped, you can fully remove the filter.

### Step 5: Clean & Check 🧼🔍
1. Clear Debris: Rinse the filter under the tap and remove any lint, coins, or hair.
2. Check Inside: Shine a torch into the hole where the filter was. Look for any objects stuck in the pump impeller (the little fan-like part inside). You can gently spin it with your finger to ensure it moves freely.
3. Reassemble: Screw the clean filter back in tightly (hand-tight is enough, don’t over-tighten!).

### Step 6: Test It 🧪✅
1. Plug the machine back in.
2. Select a "Drain & Spin" cycle or just "Spin."
3. Listen for the pump running normally. If it drains and spins without error codes, you’re good to go!

If it still hums but doesn’t drain after cleaning the filter, the pump itself might be faulty. But 90% of the time, this is all it takes! Let me know if you get stuck.
ok unplugged it. found a small hose thing like you said, doing it now with a tray. what do I do if it's still humming after?

If it’s still humming after you’ve cleared the filter and drained the water, it usually means the pump is trying to work but can’t move the water. Here are the next steps:

### 1. Check for a Hidden Obstruction 🕵️‍♂️
Even if the filter was clean, something might be stuck inside the pump housing (the hole you just cleaned).
• Shine a torch into the hole.
• Look for small items like coins, bra wires, or buttons that may have slipped past the filter.
• If you see something, try to gently fish it out with tweezers or pliers.

### 2. Test the Pump Impeller 🌀
• With the filter removed and the machine unplugged, reach into the pump housing (wear gloves if it’s sharp inside!).
• Try to spin the little fan-like wheel (the impeller) with your finger.
• If it spins freely: The pump motor might be failing electrically.
• If it’s stuck or hard to turn: Something is jammed inside, or the pump bearings are seized.

### 3. Check the Drain Hose Again 🚿
• Sometimes the blockage isn’t in the machine but further down the hose leading to your sink/standpipe.
• Disconnect the other end of the drain hose (where it goes into the wall/sink) and check for clogs.

### 4. The "Hum" Might Be a Faulty Pump ⚙️
If the impeller spins freely but the machine still hums and doesn’t drain, the pump motor is likely dead.
• Cost to Fix: A replacement pump for a Hotpoint WMBF944P typically costs £25–£40 online (e.g., Sparesbox, PartMaster).
• Difficulty: It’s usually a DIY job if you’re comfortable using a screwdriver. You’ll need to tilt the machine back and remove the bottom panel or rear panel to access it.

### 5. Consider the Age & Value ⏳
Your machine is 12 years old.
• If the pump needs replacing, weigh the cost of parts (£30) + your time vs. buying a new machine (~£300–£400).
• At 12 years old, other components (like the motor or PCB) could fail soon after this one does.

### Next Step:
Try spinning the impeller by hand. If it’s stuck, try to free it. If it spins freely but the machine still hums and won’t drain, you’ll likely need a new pump.
